lines.text: Here is a quick tour of the seven tools your agent gets when it connects to Agent R Q.
First, task. It gets the next piece of work, updates the status, and replies to you.
Memory saves what the agent learned, so the next agent starts with the notes the last one wrote.
Skills holds the playbooks, step by step guides the agent loads when a task matches.
Pano holds the shared docs, so humans and agents read and write the same pages.
Site tools reach the websites you choose to share, so the agent can use them like any other tool.
Workspace tells the agent where it is, which project, which rules, and what it may do.
And help explains every action of the other six, so the agent never has to guess.
All seven arrive with a single line of config, and no extra servers to run.
Task, memory, skills, pano, site tools, workspace, and help. That is the full set.
Agents call them on their own, without you pasting context or reminding them what to do.
Which of these seven would you use first? Tell us, or connect your agent at Agent R Q dot com.
